geo.title: Get started
geo.body:
Write a definition of "kite"; classmates hunt for counterexamples.

Goal: I can test whether a definition is a good one by checking both directions.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
A good definition works in both directions, so it can be written as a biconditional: "p if and only if q," meaning both "if p, then q" and "if q, then p" are true.

Try defining a kite as "a quadrilateral with two pairs of equal sides." A classmate points to a parallelogram: it has two pairs of equal sides, but they are opposite sides. Better: a kite is a quadrilateral with two pairs of equal consecutive sides. Test a definition by hunting for a figure that fits the words but is not the thing, or is the thing but does not fit the words.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html: Is this a good definition: A right angle is an angle that measures 90 degrees? Write it as a biconditional.
slides.reveal: Yes. An angle is a right angle if and only if it measures 90 degrees; both directions are true.
